metadata.note: The Tallulah Falls Railway, Cornelia GA - Tallulah Falls - Clayton - Dillard - Franklin NC (57-58 mi), and its predecessors on Cornelia - Tallulah Falls: the Northeastern Railroad of Georgia (Richmond and Danville-controlled, opened c.1882) and the Blue Ridge and Atlantic Railroad (1888-1898). Features split at each operator change under Rule 4 (Northeastern -> BR&A 1888; BR&A -> TFR 1898), sharing identical geometry on Cornelia - Tallulah Falls; the TFR is split by extension because each piece has its own drawable start. The Southern Railway's 1905 purchase of the TFR's stock is NOT a split - the TFR ran its own trains under its own name and receivers. Each drawn span is the research report's drawable: span. Passenger service ended 1946; the 1946-1961 freight-only years are not drawn.
sources: John Fowler, Georgia Railroads Passenger Stations (branchline.uk), table 23: https://www.branchline.uk/jfpdf/georgiarrs.pdf
Chronicling America (Library of Congress): Savannah Morning News 1883, 1889, 1890, 1904; Keowee Courier 1904, 1905, 1907; Cherokee Scout 1908; Farmer and Mechanic 1907
not_yet_sourced: Who to name for 1882-1888 (Rules 4/6): drawn as the Northeastern Railroad of Georgia, the corporate operator named in the 1883 source. Whether its trains were advertised as Richmond and Danville is unresolved; the R&D already exists in data/ as 'Richmond and Danville Railroad' (#5D4A7A). If R&D advertising is found, recolour/relabel northeastern-ga-cornelia-tallulah-falls to the R&D.
[ANCHOR] northeastern-ga-cornelia-tallulah-falls: only 1884 proven (1884 Official Guide via Fowler). Opening c.1882 and 1885-1887 have no passenger sighting.

[OPEN] blue-ridge-atlantic-cornelia-tallulah-falls: confirmed only 1889-1890; 1888 and 1891-1898 (receivership 1893-1897) have no positive passenger sighting. 1893 Official Guide, ICC valuation docket and Foxfire's 'Memories of a Mountain Shortline' (1976) are the likeliest sources.
[OPEN START] tfr-cornelia-tallulah-falls: start bracket 1898-1904, drawn from the first confirmed year 1904.

[OPEN START] tfr-dillard-franklin: start bracket 1907-1908 (Wikipedia June 1907 vs contemporary reports of grading June 1907 and rails not into the Franklin depot Nov 1907); drawn from 1908. If June 1907 refers to Otto or the state line, a Dillard - Otto piece could start 1907 - no dated evidence.

tfr-tallulah-falls-clayton start: 1904 (rabunhistory.org, abandonedrails.com) vs 1905 (first confirmed passenger train north of Tallulah Falls); drawn 1905. A mid-1904 Atlanta Constitution report of the first train to Clayton would move it to 1904.
Passenger end day: 31 Jul 1946 (rabunhistory.org) vs May 1946 (abandonedrails.com); year agreed. No post-1946 mixed train found, but 1946-1961 newspapers were not searched in depth.
Headways and average speeds throughout are estimates; no TFR timetable was read.
Geometry: whether the 1910-1927 hydro reservoirs forced any relocation of the line, and the location of the original (1882-1903) Tallulah Falls terminus and of the Franklin depot, were not checked.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Built 2026-11-09 to Rule 1: the TFR's 1946-1961 freight-only years and the post-1961 Southern/NS Cornelia - Clarkesville freight spur are not drawn; the Burton Junction dam construction line and other hydro-construction trackage (1910-1926) are excluded as freight/construction.
metadata.horsecar_audit: None: steam from opening (c.1882); diesel 1948, after passenger service ended.
metadata.line_label_audit: Labels written to Rule 6 at creation, 2026-11-09.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] 1884 is the single proven passenger year: Fowler's Georgia station list gives 'Turnerville [Turnersville q]', q = the 1884 Official Guide, i.e. a passenger stop in 1884. Service certainly ran wider both ways - the branch opened c.1882 (Wikipedia, rabunhistory.org; the Savannah Morning News of 22 Nov 1883 says G. J. Foreacre had 'carried the Northeastern Railroad to Tallulah Falls', a construction statement) and passed to the Blue Ridge and Atlantic early 1888 - but no other year is confirmed. Do not widen without a dated passenger sighting. Operated by the Northeastern Railroad of Georgia under Richmond and Danville control (R&D bought it 1881); whether trains were advertised as Northeastern or R&D is unresolved (see metadata.not_yet_sourced). headway_min is an ESTIMATE (no timetable read for this era), and avg_speed_kmh is an unsourced estimate.

segments.note: [OPEN both ends] Drawn only across the two years with dated passenger sightings: Savannah Morning News 1 Sep 1889 p2 (Atlanta, 31 Aug: two passengers hurt in 'a smash-up on the Blue Ridge and Atlantic road ... All of them were in the smoking car'; the dispatch places it 'near Rabun Gap', beyond the BR&A's railhead, so the place is probably garbled) and Savannah Morning News 6 Sep 1890 p1 (the BR&A 'train from Tallulah Falls for Cornelia Junction' derailed at Hazel Creek near Demorest with ten passengers in the rear coach - a mixed train, which counts). 1889 is the first CONFIRMED year and 1890 the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known start or end: the BR&A bought the branch early 1888 and was sold at foreclosure 7 Nov 1897 (Tallulah Falls Railway organized March 1898), and service very probably ran the whole decade (receiver from 1893), but no 1888 or 1891-1898 passenger sighting was found. A June/July 1896 resort ad naming Cornelia 'at junction of Blue Ridge and Atlantic railway' does not itself state a train ran and is not counted. Do not extend without evidence. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (no timetable read for this era), and avg_speed_kmh is an unsourced estimate.

segments.note: [OPEN start] 1904 is the earliest CONFIRMED Tallulah Falls Railway-era passenger year, NOT a known start: the Keowee Courier of 20 Jul 1904 p2 announces 'Smith's annual excursion to Tallulah Falls' leaving Westminster SC on 21 July, a rail excursion that could only reach Tallulah Falls over this line from Cornelia ('annual' implies earlier years, none dated). The TFR was organized March 1898 to buy the foreclosed Blue Ridge and Atlantic, so the bracket for the start is 1898-1904; 1898-1903 are withheld for want of a dated passenger sighting. Do not extend earlier without evidence. Passenger service ended in 1946 - a stated ending, agreed by rabunhistory.org ('abruptly and permanently ended on July 31, 1946', after engine No. 73 struck a log truck) and abandonedrails.com ('ended abruptly in May of 1946'); the DAY is disputed, the year is not. Freight continued until the last run on 25 Mar 1961 (Southern bought Cornelia - Clarkesville as a freight spur; rails north of Clarkesville lifted by early 1962) - those freight-only years are not drawn (Rule 1). No post-1946 mixed train was found. The Southern Railway held the TFR's stock from 1905, but the TFR ran its own trains under its own name and receivers (1908; 1923-1961), so this is not an operator split. headway_min (about two trains each way a day) is an ESTIMATE, not read from a timetable; avg_speed_kmh is an unsourced estimate.

Wikipedia's 'North Carolina State line was reached early in 1904' is contradicted by the 1904-05 newspapers. No post-1946 mixed train was found.
